references.text: Jeremiah 25:8–9 describes how the Lord sends Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, against his people and surrounding nations to destroy them, paralleling how the servants are mistreated and killed in Matthew 22:6.

In Exodus 32:27–28, after the Israelites made the golden calf, Moses ordered the Levites to go through the camp and kill, even among their own brothers, friends, and neighbors, reflecting the violence against the servants in Matthew 22:6.

Hosea 10:14–15 speaks of war and destruction coming upon Israel because of their sins, including violence against the innocent, which can be seen as parallel to the violence against the servants in Matthew 22:6.
Matthew 21:35–39 tells another parable where the vineyard workers mistreat and kill the sons sent to them, directly related to the mistreatment and killing of the servants in Matthew 22:6.
Luke 20:10–15 describes a situation similar to that in Matthew 21:35–39 and 22:6, where the vineyard workers mistreat and kill the heir, pointing to the same kind of violence against messengers.
